<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913771_theRebbe_98" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913771_theRebbe_98__p005">
  <section v="12">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the oath given to man is not only for making the world a dwelling place for G-d, but also grants him the power to do so, and this oath is included in the concept that man preceded creation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And perhaps one may add,</t>
    <t s="2">that this that our sages said, that the reason man was created last is so that he could enter the feast immediately,</t>
    <t s="3">the intention in this is,</t>
    <t s="4">not only regarding the world that man must make into a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="5">but also regarding the granting of power to man,</t>
    <t s="6">“they adjure him” from the term satiety</t>
    <t s="7">(the concept of a feast),</t>
    <t s="8">so that he can make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="9">And based on this, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="10">that this that man preceded the act of creation and everything was created for his sake,</t>
    <t s="11">also includes the oath.</t>
    <t s="12">For the intention of the oath,</t>
    <t s="13">the drawing down of the aspect of Atik</t>
    <t s="14">[and one could say even more than this,</t>
    <t s="15">also the intention in the aspect of Atik itself],</t>
    <t s="16">is for the sake of man’s service.</t>
    <t s="17">And through man fulfilling the oath,</t>
    <t s="18">an elevation is caused in it,</t>
    <t s="19">for the intention of the oath is completed.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="13">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the power given to man on Rosh Hashanah to the distinction between the initial will and delight in creation stemming from G-d's own nature versus that which comes through man's service, revealing the purpose of creation for Israel.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">9)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, this that was explained above</t>
    <t s="2">(section 7)</t>
    <t s="3">that on Rosh Hashanah a granting of power is drawn down to man to act upon the world and make it a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="4">can be connected with what is explained in many places,</t>
    <t s="5">that at the beginning of creation,</t>
    <t s="6">the drawing down of the will and delight in the creation of the worlds was from His own side,</t>
    <t s="7">for He desires kindness,</t>
    <t s="8">and the drawing down of the will and delight in the creation of the world now is through the service of man.</t>
    <t s="9">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="10">that this distinction is not only in the manner of the drawing down</t>
    <t s="11">(whether the drawing down is from His own side or whether the drawing down is through the service of man)</t>
    <t s="12">but also in the will and delight themselves.</t>
    <t s="13">For the will and delight in the creation of the worlds that stems from “He desires kindness” is in the creation of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="14">through which His kindness, blessed be He, is revealed,</t>
    <t s="15">and the will and delight in the creation of the worlds that comes through the service of man is that the Holy One, blessed be He, desired to have a dwelling place for Himself, blessed be He, in the lower realms,</t>
    <t s="16">and that the making of the dwelling place would be through the service of man.</t>
    <t s="17">And through the revelation of this delight in the creation of the worlds,</t>
    <t s="18">that the intention of the creation of the worlds is for the sake of Israel,</t>
    <t s="19">there is power in man</t>
    <t s="20">(“you are called ‘man’”)</t>
    <t s="21">to act upon creation and make a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="22">For this that was explained above, that the granting of power to man to act upon creation is the revelation of the root of the soul</t>
    <t s="23">(the concept of the oath),</t>
    <t s="24">is in relation to man.</t>
    <t s="25">And the action that is done in the world through the service of man</t>
    <t s="26">(that through the service of man the world becomes a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He)</t>
    <t s="27">is through the revelation of the intention of creation,</t>
    <t s="28">that the creation of the world is for the sake of Israel.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="14">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that even on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat, the service of reciting the Shofar verses is essential because the revelation of delight grants man the power to make the world a dwelling place.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">10)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is the law:</t>
    <t s="2">And based on this, it can be explained that even on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat, the superiority of the service exists,</t>
    <t s="3">for the intention in the drawing down of the delight</t>
    <t s="4">[and also in the delight itself]</t>
    <t s="5">is for the sake of man,</t>
    <t s="6">that through the delight there will be a granting of power to man to make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He</t>
    <t s="7">(in the manner explained above in section 8 regarding the oath),</t>
    <t s="8">for the granting of power to man is specifically when the drawing down of the delight is in revelation.</t>
    <t s="9">And since even on Rosh Hashanah that falls on Shabbat, the revelation of the delight is through the recitation of the Shofar verses</t>
    <t s="10">(as explained above in section 2 from the continuation of 5666),</t>
    <t s="11">it follows,</t>
    <t s="12">that even the service of reciting the Shofar verses is relevant to an essential matter.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
